candidates.text: When a scheduler splits a daily time budget across windows, it should allocate demand exactly when total candidate demand fits the daily budget rather than enforcing an artificial proportional split that can reject feasible combinations.
candidates.rationale: Story 016 was triggered by a 45-minute Laundry + Clean kitchen combination being rejected from a 60-minute day because proportional budgeting gave morning only ~1 minute. The fix and review both confirm that demand-aware allocation is needed to keep feasible days from cascading into overflow.

candidates.text: When falling back from a preferred time window, prefer the nearest window before jumping to a distant one.
candidates.rationale: Review finding 4 noted that a fixed morning→afternoon→evening fallback order could place an evening task in morning even when afternoon had room. Proximity-aware fallback respects user expectations for time-of-day preferences.
